chunks: Al-Ṣādiq, peace be upon him, was asked about a well from which water was drawn, then wudu (ablution) was performed with it, clothes were washed with it, and dough was kneaded with it; then it was learned that there had been a dead animal in it.
So he said: “There is no harm, and the garment is not to be washed because of it, nor is the salat (prayer) to be repeated because of it.”

key_terms.الثِّيَابُ: the clothes that were washed with the water
key_terms.بِئْرٍ: a well from which water is drawn
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm or legal problem
key_terms.مَيْتَةٌ: a dead animal or carcass found in the well
key_terms.وَعُجِنَ: dough was kneaded using the water

ai.seo_question: If a dead animal is later discovered in a well, must wudu (ablution), washed clothes, or salat (prayer) be repeated?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning water drawn from a well that was later discovered to have contained a dead animal. Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام states that there is no harm in what was previously done with that water, and neither the clothing must be rewashed nor the salat (prayer) repeated.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.20 - Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) was asked about a well from which water was drawn for ablution, washing clothes, and kneading dough, and then it was discovered that there was a dead animal in it.
Imam (as) said: "There is no harm, and the clothes do not need to be washed again, nor does the prayer need to be repeated”.
